1: 1 The proverbs of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel, <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
To know wisdom and instruction; To comprehend the words of understanding; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
To receive the discipline of wisdom, Justice, and right, and equity; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
To give prudence to the simple, To the young man knowledge and discretion; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
That the wise man may hear, and increase in learning, And the man of understanding may attain unto wise counsels; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
To understand a proverb, and a figure; The words of the wise, and their dark sayings. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge; But the foolish despise wisdom and discipline. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Hear, my son, the instruction of thy father, And forsake not the teaching of thy mother; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For they shall be a chaplet of grace unto thy head, And chains about thy neck. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
My son, if sinners entice thee, Consent thou not. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
If they say: 'Come with us, Let us lie in wait for blood, Let us lurk for the innocent without cause; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Let us swallow them up alive as the grave, And whole, as those that go down into the pit; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
We shall find all precious substance, We shall fill our houses with spoil; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Cast in thy lot among us; Let us all have one purse'— <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
My son, walk not thou in the way with them, Restrain thy foot from their path; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For their feet run to evil, And they make haste to shed blood. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For in vain the net is spread In the eyes of any bird; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
And these lie in wait for their own blood, They lurk for their own lives. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
So are the ways of every one that is greedy of gain; It taketh away the life of the owners thereof. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Wisdom crieth aloud in the street, She uttereth her voice in the broad places; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
She calleth at the head of the noisy streets, At the entrances of the gates, in the city, she uttereth her words: <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
How long, ye thoughtless, will ye love thoughtlessness? And how long will scorners delight them in scorning, And fools hate knowledge? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Turn you at my reproof; Behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you,  ​ I will make known my words unto you. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Because I have called, and ye refused, I have stretched out my hand, and no man attended, <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
But ye have set at nought all my counsel, And would none of my reproof; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
I also, in your calamity, will laugh, I will mock when your dread cometh; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
When your dread cometh as a storm, And your calamity cometh on as a whirlwind; When trouble and distress come upon you. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Then will they call me, but I will not answer, They will seek me earnestly, but they shall not find me. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For that they hated knowledge, And did not choose the fear of the Lord ; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
They would none of my counsel, They despised all my reproof. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, And be filled with their own devices. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For the waywardness of the thoughtless shall slay them, And the confidence of fools shall destroy them. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
But whoso hearkeneth unto me shall dwell securely, And shall be quiet without fear of evil.' <span class="anchor"
2: 2 My son, if thou wilt receive my words, And lay up my commandments with thee; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
So that thou make thine ear attend unto wisdom, And thy heart incline to discernment; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Yea, if thou call for understanding, And lift up thy voice for discernment; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
If thou seek her as silver, And search for her as for hid treasures; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Then shalt thou understand the fear of the Lord , And find the knowledge of God. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For the Lord giveth wisdom, Out of His mouth cometh knowledge and discernment; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
He layeth up sound wisdom for the upright, He is a shield to them that walk in integrity; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
That He may guard the paths of justice, And preserve the way of His godly ones. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Then shalt thou understand righteousness and justice, And equity, yea, every good path. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For wisdom shall enter into thy heart, And knowledge shall be pleasant unto thy soul; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Discretion shall watch over thee, Discernment shall guard thee; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
To deliver thee from the way of evil, From the men that speak froward things; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Who leave the paths of uprightness, To walk in the ways of darkness; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Who rejoice to do evil, And delight in the frowardness of evil; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Who are crooked in their ways, And perverse in their paths; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
To deliver thee from the strange woman, Even from the alien woman that maketh smooth her words; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
That forsaketh the lord of her youth, And forgetteth the covenant of her God.  ​ <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For her house sinketh down unto death, And her paths unto the shades; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
None that go unto her return, Neither do they attain unto the paths of life; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
That thou mayest walk in the way of good men, And keep the paths of the righteous. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For the upright shall dwell in the land, And the whole-hearted shall remain in it. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
But the wicked shall be cut off from the land, And the faithless shall be plucked up out of it. <span class="anchor"
3: 3 My son, forget not my teaching; But let thy heart keep my commandments; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For length of days, and years of life, And peace, will they add to thee. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Let not kindness and truth forsake thee; Bind them about thy neck, write them upon the table of thy heart; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
So shalt thou find grace and good favour In the sight of God and man. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Trust in the Lord with all thy heart, And lean not upon thine own understanding. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
In all thy ways acknowledge Him, And He will direct thy paths. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Be not wise in thine own eyes; Fear the Lord , and depart from evil; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
It shall be health to thy navel, And marrow to thy bones. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Honour the Lord with thy substance, And with the first-fruits of all thine increase; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
So shall thy barns be filled with plenty, And thy vats shall overflow with new wine. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord , Neither spurn thou His correction; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For whom the Lord loveth He correcteth, Even as a father the son in whom he delighteth. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Happy is the man that findeth wisdom, And the man that obtaineth understanding. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For the merchandise of it is better than the merchandise of silver, And the gain thereof than fine gold. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
She is more precious than rubies; And all the things thou canst desire are not to be compared unto her. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Length of days is in her right hand; In her left hand are riches and honour. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Her ways are ways of pleasantness, And all her paths are peace. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
She is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her, And happy is every one that holdest her fast. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The Lord by wisdom founded the earth; By understanding He established the heavens. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
By His knowledge the depths were broken up, And the skies drop down the dew. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
My son, let not them depart from thine eyes; Keep sound wisdom and discretion; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
So shall they be life unto thy soul, And grace to thy neck.  ​ <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Then shalt thou walk in thy way securely, And thou shalt not dash thy foot. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid; Yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Be not afraid of sudden terror, Neither of the destruction of the wicked, when it cometh; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For the Lord will be thy confidence, And will keep thy foot from being caught. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Withhold not good from him to whom it is due, When it is in the power of thy hand to do it. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Say not unto thy neighbour: 'Go, and come again, And to-morrow I will give'; when thou hast it by thee. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Devise not evil against thy neighbour, Seeing he dwelleth securely by thee. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Strive not with a man without cause, If he have done thee no harm. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Envy thou not the man of violence, And choose none of his ways. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For the perverse is an abomination to the Lord ; But His counsel is with the upright. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The curse of the Lord is in the house of the wicked; But He blesseth the habitation of the righteous. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
If it concerneth the scorners, He scorneth them, But unto the humble He giveth grace. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The wise shall inherit honour; But as for the fools, they carry away shame. <span class="anchor"
4: 4 Hear, ye children, the instruction of a father, And attend to know understanding. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For I give you good doctrine; Forsake ye not my teaching. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For I was a son unto my father, Tender and an only one in the sight of my mother. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
And he taught me, and said unto me: 'Let thy heart hold fast my words, Keep my commandments, and live; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Get wisdom, get understanding; Forget not, neither decline from the words of my mouth; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Forsake her not, and she will preserve thee; Love her, and she will keep thee. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The beginning of wisdom is: Get wisdom; Yea, with all thy getting get understanding. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Extol her, and she will exalt thee; She will bring thee to honour, when thou dost embrace her. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
She will give to thy head a chaplet of grace; A crown of glory will she bestow on thee.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Hear, O my son, and receive my sayings; And the years of thy life shall be many. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
I have taught thee in the way of wisdom; I have led thee in paths of uprightness. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
When thou goest, thy step shall not be straitened; And if thou runnest, thou shalt not stumble. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Take fast hold of instruction, let her not go; Keep her, for she is thy life. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Enter not into the path of the wicked, And walk not in the way of evil men.  ​ <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Avoid it, pass not by it; Turn from it, and pass on. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For they sleep not, except they have done evil; And their sleep is taken away, unless they cause some to fall. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For they eat the bread of wickedness, And drink the wine of violence. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
But the path of the righteous is as the light of dawn, That shineth more and more unto the perfect day. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The way of the wicked is as darkness; They know not at what they stumble. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
My son, attend to my words; Incline thine ear unto my sayings. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Let them not depart from thine eyes; Keep them in the midst of thy heart. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For they are life unto those that find them, And health to all their flesh. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Above all that thou guardest keep thy heart; For out of it are the issues of life. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Put away from thee a froward mouth, And perverse lips put far from thee. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Let thine eyes look right on, And let thine eyelids look straight before thee. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Make plain the path of thy feet, And let all thy ways be established. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Turn not to the right hand nor to the left; Remove thy foot from evil. <span class="anchor"
5: 5 My son, attend unto my wisdom; Incline thine ear to my understanding; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
That thou mayest preserve discretion, And that thy lips may keep knowledge. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For the lips of a strange woman drop honey, And her mouth is smoother than oil; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
But her end is bitter as wormwood, Sharp as a two-edged sword. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Her feet go down to death; Her steps take hold on the nether-world; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Lest she should walk the even path of life, Her ways wander, but she knoweth it not. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Now therefore, O ye children, hearken unto me, And depart not from the words of my mouth. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Remove thy way far from her, And come not nigh the door of her house; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Lest thou give thy vigour unto others, And thy years unto the cruel; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Lest strangers be filled with thy strength, And thy labours be in the house of an alien; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
And thou moan, when thine end cometh, When thy flesh and thy body are consumed, <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
And say: 'How have I hated instruction, And my heart despised reproof; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Neither have I hearkened to the voice of my teachers, Nor inclined mine ear to them that instructed me! <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
I was well nigh in all evil In the midst of the congregation and assembly.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Drink waters out of thine own cistern,  ​ And running waters out of thine own well. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Let thy springs be dispersed abroad, And courses of water in the streets. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Let them be only thine own, And not strangers' with thee. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Let thy fountain be blessed; And have joy of the wife of thy youth. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
A lovely hind and a graceful doe, Let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; With her love be thou ravished always. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Why then wilt thou, my son, be ravished with a strange woman, And embrace the bosom of an alien? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For the ways of man are before the eyes of the Lord , And He maketh even all his paths. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
His own iniquities shall ensnare the wicked, And he shall be holden with the cords of his sin. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
He shall die for lack of instruction; And in the greatness of his folly he shall reel. <span class="anchor"
6: 6 My son, if thou art become surety for thy neighbour, If thou hast struck thy hands for a stranger— <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Thou art snared by the words of thy mouth, Thou art caught by the words of thy mouth— <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Do this now, my son, and deliver thyself, Seeing thou art come into the hand of thy neighbour; Go, humble thyself, and urge thy neighbour. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Give not sleep to thine eyes, nor slumber to thine eyelids. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Deliver thyself as a gazelle from the hand [of the hunter], And as a bird from the hand of the fowler. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Go to the ant, thou sluggard; Consider her ways, and be wise; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Which having no chief, Overseer, or ruler, <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Provideth her bread in the summer, And gatherest her food in the harvest. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard? When wilt thou arise out of thy sleep? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, A little folding of the hands to sleep'— <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
So shall thy poverty come as a runner, And thy want as an armed man. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
A base person, a man of iniquity, Is he that walketh with a froward mouth; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
That winketh with his eyes, that scrapeth with his feet, That pointeth with his fingers; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Frowardness is in his heart, he deviseth evil continually; He soweth discord. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Therefore shall his calamity come suddenly; On a sudden shall he be broken, and that without remedy. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
There are six things which the Lord hateth, Yea, seven which are an abomination unto Him: <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, And hands that shed innocent blood; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
A heart that deviseth wicked thoughts, Feet that are swift in running to evil; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
A false witness that breatheth out lies,  ​ And he that soweth discord among brethren. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
My son, keep the commandment of thy father, And forsake not the teaching of thy mother; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Bind them continually upon thy heart, Tie them about thy neck. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
When thou walkest, it shall lead thee, When thou liest down, it shall watch over thee; And when thou awakest, it shall talk with thee. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For the commandment is a lamp, and the teaching is light, And reproofs of instruction are the way of life; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
To keep thee from the evil woman, From the smoothness of the alien tongue. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Lust not after her beauty in thy heart; Neither let her captivate thee with her eyelids. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For on account of a harlot a man is brought to a loaf of bread, But the adulteress hunteth for the precious life. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Can a man take fire in his bosom, And his clothes not be burned? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Or can one walk upon hot coals, And his feet not be scorched? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
So he that goeth in to his neighbour's wife; Whosoever toucheth her shall not go unpunished. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Men do not despise a thief, if he steal To satisfy his soul when he is hungry; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
But if he be found, he must restore sevenfold, He must give all the substance of his house. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
He that committeth adultery with a woman lacketh understanding; He doeth it that would destroy his own soul. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Wounds and dishonour shall he get, And his reproach shall not be wiped away. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For jealousy is the rage of a man, And he will not spare in the day of vengeance. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
He will not regard any ransom; Neither will he rest content, though thou givest many gifts. <span class="anchor"
7: 7 My son, keep my words, And lay up my commandments with thee. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Keep my commandments and live, And my teaching as the apple of thine eye. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Bind them upon thy fingers, Write them upon the table of thy heart. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Say unto wisdom: 'Thou art my sister', And call understanding thy kinswoman; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
That they may keep thee from the strange woman, From the alien woman that maketh smooth her words. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For at the window of my house I looked forth through my lattice; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
And I beheld among the thoughtless ones, I discerned among the youths, A young man void of understanding, <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Passing through the street near her corner, And he went the way to her house; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
In the twilight, in the evening of the day, In the blackness of night and the darkness. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
And, behold, there met him a woman  ​ With the attire of a harlot, and wily of heart. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
She is riotous and rebellious, Her feet abide not in her house; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Now she is in the streets, now in the broad places, And lieth in wait at every corner. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
So she caught him, and kissed him, And with an impudent face she said unto him: <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Sacrifices of peace-offerings were due from me; This day have I paid my vows. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Therefore came I forth to meet thee, To seek thy face, and I have found thee. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
I have decked my couch with coverlets, With striped cloths of the yarn of Egypt. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
I have perfumed my bed With myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning; Let us solace ourselves with loves. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For my husband is not at home, He is gone a long journey; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
He hath taken the bag of money with him; He will come home at the full moon.' <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
With her much fair speech she causeth him to yield, With the blandishment of her lips she enticeth him away. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
He goeth after her straightway, As an ox that goeth to the slaughter, Or as one in fetters to the correction of the fool; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Till an arrow strike through his liver; As a bird hasteneth to the snare— And knoweth not that it is at the cost of his life. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Now therefore, O ye children, hearken unto me, And attend to the words of my mouth. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Let not thy heart decline to her ways, Go not astray in her paths. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For she hath cast down many wounded; Yea, a mighty host are all her slain. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Her house is the way to the nether-world, Going down to the chambers of death. <span class="anchor"
8: 8 Doth not wisdom call, And understanding put forth her voice? <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
In the top of high places by the way, Where the paths meet, she standeth; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Beside the gates, at the entry of the city, At the coming in at the doors, she crieth aloud: <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Unto you, O men, I call, And my voice is to the sons of men. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
O ye thoughtless, understand prudence, And, ye fools, be ye of an understanding heart. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Hear, for I will speak excellent things, And the opening of my lips shall be right things. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For my mouth shall utter truth, And wickedness is an abomination to my lips. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
All the words of my mouth are in righteousness, There is nothing perverse or crooked in them. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
They are all plain to him that understandeth, And right to them that find knowledge. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Receive my instruction, and not silver, And knowledge rather than choice gold.  ​ <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
For wisdom is better than rubies, And all things desirable are not to be compared unto her. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
I wisdom dwell with prudence, And find out knowledge of devices. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The fear of the Lord is to hate evil; Pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, And the froward mouth, do I hate. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom; I am understanding, power is mine. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
By me kings reign, And princes decree justice. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
By me princes rule, And nobles, even all the judges of the earth. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
I love them that love me, And those that seek me earnestly shall find me. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Riches and honour are with me; Yea, enduring riches and righteousness. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"

And I have not learned wisdom, That I should have the knowledge of the Holy One. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"

The locusts have no king, Yet go they forth all of them by bands; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The spider thou canst take with the hands, Yet is she in kings' palaces. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
There are three things which are stately in their march, Yea, four which are stately in going: <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
The lion, which is mightiest among beasts, And turneth not away for any; <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"

Give not thy strength unto women, Nor thy ways to that which destroyeth kings. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"

Let him drink, and forget his poverty, And remember his misery no more. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Open thy mouth for the dumb, In the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction. <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"

She maketh for herself coverlets; Her clothing is fine linen and purple. נ <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Her husband is known in the gates, When he sitteth among the elders of the land. ס <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
She maketh linen garments and selleth them; And delivereth girdles unto the merchant. ע <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Strength and dignity are her clothing; And she laugheth at the time to come. פ <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"

Grace is deceitful, and beauty is vain; But a woman that feareth the Lord , she shall be praised. ת <span class="wst-verse wst-verse-float"
Give her of the fruit of her hands; And let her works praise her in the gates.  ↑ Heb. Lemoel .
